To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) an intermediate SU(2)L ×SU(2) R×SU(4)c symmetry is all that’s necessary for unification of α and αs and for unification of sin2θw, b) the intermediate mass scale is 1014 GeV and the GUT scale is 1017 GeV, and c) the unification of sin 2θW requires the introduction of a new parameter in the theory.

the two-loop renormalization group equations of the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM), with a Pati–Salm intermediate symmetry, are consistent with the empirical values of αs(MZ), α(MZ) and sin2 θw (MZ) provided that the intermediate symmetry breaking scale is high, MINT ≳1014 GeV, and the unification scale is correspondingly higher, MUNIF ≳ 1017 GeV.

the two-loop unification of the gauge couplings of the Standard Model is possible in an intermediate SU(2)L × SU(2)R × SU(4) Pati–Salem group if the intermediate scale is 1014 GeV, and that the unification of the three gauge couplings is also possible in a minimal SU(5) group if the GUT scale is 1017 GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (i) The unification of the gauge couplings in the standard model at the GUT scale, (ii) The unification scale, (iii) The gauge couplings at the unification scale.
the unification of the Standard Model gauge couplings and with the determination of the intermediate scale of the Pati–SALAM symmetry.
the unification of couplings in supersymmetric models with an intermediate Pati–SALAM group and with a high mass scale for the intermediate group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intermediate Pati–SALAM symmetry group is a viable alternative to the conventional SU(5) grand unified theory.
, at the present level of precision, a Pati–Salem intermediate symmetry group is a necessary and sufficient ingredient for a consistent unification of the standard model with gravity.
the intermediate mass scale is not a necessary condition for the unification of the three couplings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unification of the three gauge couplings in the Standard Model can be accomplished with a high intermediate mass scale and that the unification scale is not necessarily a fundamental mass scale.
the intermediate Pati–SALAM level is the only one of the three possible intermediate levels (SU(3)L×SU(3)R×SU(N) and SU(3)C×SU(2)L×U(1)Y) that is consistent with the data.

the intermediate Pati–SALAM group is a viable unifying group for the standard model gauge group, and that the intermediate mass scale is a necessary and sufficient condition for a successful unification of the gauge couplings.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high intermediate scale and high GUT scale are both consequences of the intermediate Pati–SALAM symmetry and that the latter is the only new symmetry that is necessary to explain the observed value of sin2θw.

the intermediate Pati–SALAM group is a viable alternative to a conventional GUT group, such as SO(10), in the sense that it can accommodate empirical values of the electroweak couplings and sin2θW(MZ) within an extended unification context.
, if one insists on a unification of the gauge couplings at the GUT scale, the only viable way to achieve this is to embed the standard model in a Pati–Salm group at a lower energy scale.
